case: PostgreSQL numeric[] XLSX re-import through Gnumeric
contract: PostgreSQL's numeric[] contains a 40-digit integer, a high-scale decimal, scale-preserving 1.2300, NaN, positive and negative Infinity, and SQL NULL.
The native test checks pg_typeof, native numeric[] text, array_to_json, array_send, and the exact rebound values and wire bytes.
BookiE writes the array as a text cell in source.xlsx; Gnumeric preserves the exact text as an ODS string cell and an XLSX inline string through XLSX/ODS/XLSX re-save.
No formula is created in source.xlsx, the ODS workbook, or the re-saved XLSX workbook.

native_export_test.command: rtk proxy env BOOKIEE_XLSX_REIMPORT_ARTIFACT=<absolute-evidence-dir>/source.xlsx cargo test --offline --locked -p tablepro-driver-postgres --test integration array_contract::value_contract_numeric_array_file_exports_preserve_exact_text -- --ignored --exact --test-threads=1

steps: Install Gnumeric in the pinned Debian image.

consumer_assertions.method: Python standard-library ZIP/XML checks require the exact expected A2 text, XLSX shared or inline string type, ODS string type, and no formulas in any artifact.
consumer_assertions.result: Exact numeric[] text preserved across all three artifacts; no formulas.

remaining: Other PostgreSQL array types, file-writer/session combinations, spreadsheet applications, and the broader B3 matrix remain open.
